anti_overlap: fd-ecs-determinism-epithets covers runtime tick-order and float determinism — this agent covers on-disk serialization format and schema evolution
fd-salience-decay-tuning covers whether salience numbers are well-calibrated — this agent covers whether salience survives save/load intact
fd-event-reactor-completeness covers trigger hook availability — this agent covers what happens to earned epithets in the save file after they are awarded
decision_lens: The brainstorm defers LexemeId allocation to implementation and introduces a HashMap<LexemeId, Lexeme> with stub enum variants for Saying/Proverb/Slang — the trade-off is extensibility vs. save-schema fragility. Adding a new variant to LexemeKind is a breaking change if the enum uses default serde tagging and old saves contain unknown variant tags.
focus: Serialization stability of ColonyLexicon and Epithets across saves, LexemeId allocation scheme correctness, and schema evolution strategy for future LexemeKind variants
name: fd-save-schema-stability
persona: Apply the perspective of a Rust serialization architect who specializes in serde schema evolution in long-lived save games — they care about whether adding a new LexemeKind variant or a new Epithets field silently corrupts or silently ignores data in saves from a prior version; they measure by asking 'does a save from version N load correctly in version N+1 without data loss or panic?'; they flag any enum without a serde unknown-variant fallback or any id allocation scheme that reuses ids across reloads.
review_areas: Specify the LexemeId allocation scheme: the brainstorm does not define whether LexemeId is a monotonic u64 counter, a content-hash, or a UUID — if it is a monotonic counter stored on GameWorld, verify it is persisted in the save and not re-derived at load (re-derivation would reassign ids, breaking Epithets.earned references)

Audit whether Epithets.earned: Vec<EarnedEpithet> stores LexemeId as a foreign key into ColonyLexicon — if the lexicon entry is missing at load (e.g., from a save truncation or schema migration), confirm the load path degrades gracefully rather than panicking on unwrap

Evaluate serde tagging on LexemeKind: if the enum uses the default serde internally-tagged or adjacently-tagged representation, adding Saying/Proverb/Slang variants in a future sprint requires that old saves (with only Epithet entries) continue to deserialize correctly — recommend an explicit tag attribute with documented variant names or document the migration path

Check whether ColonyLexicon as a field on GameWorld inherits GameWorld's serde derive or requires its own — if world.rs:178-245 uses a manual serialize impl, adding the lexicon field requires updating that impl; if it uses derive, adding the field with serde default attribute is sufficient

Assess whether the Lexeme.text: String field creates schema stability concerns — if an epithet's canonical text changes in a future patch (e.g., 'the Defiant' renamed to 'the Unbowed'), old saves carry the old text while new game logic expects the new text; determine whether text should be stored or derived from LexemeKind at render time

Review the ElfName stability guarantee: the brainstorm explicitly chooses Epithets as a separate component to avoid ElfName schema churn — confirm that the chosen storage split (LexemeId on Epithets, text in ColonyLexicon) actually achieves this, and that no ElfName field needs to be added to support epithet display

severity_examples.condition: next_lexeme_id: u64 field omitted from GameWorld serde or initialized to 0 in Default impl instead of loaded from save
severity_examples.scenario: LexemeId is a monotonic counter not persisted in the save — on reload, the counter resets to 0 and new epithets earned post-load are assigned ids that collide with pre-save ids, causing Epithets.earned references to point to wrong lexemes silently

severity_examples.condition: LexemeKind enum lacks a serde unknown-variant fallback or skip annotation on future variants; no migration path documented
severity_examples.scenario: A future sprint adds LexemeKind::Saying — old saves with only Epithet lexemes deserialize the LexemeKind field and encounter an unknown variant tag, causing the entire ColonyLexicon to fail deserialization and the save to fail to load

severity_examples.condition: Text is stored in Lexeme rather than derived from LexemeKind::Epithet variant at render time; no migration or canonicalization step
severity_examples.scenario: Lexeme.text stores 'the Defiant' at earn time — a patch renames it to 'the Unbroken' for narrative reasons; all old saves continue displaying 'the Defiant' while new earns display 'the Unbroken', creating a split-identity colony where identical trigger outcomes produce different names based on earn date

success_hints: A save created before a new LexemeKind variant is added loads cleanly in the new version with unknown variants treated as skipped or migrated
LexemeId counter is round-tripped through save/load with a test asserting the first id after reload is max(existing ids) + 1
The ElfName struct is unchanged by this sprint — confirmed by a diff showing zero modifications to components.rs ElfName fields
task_context: The brainstorm introduces ColonyLexicon as a new GameWorld field with HashMap<LexemeId, Lexeme>, a LexemeKind enum with stub future variants, and a LexemeId foreign-key pattern on the Epithets component. This agent reviews serialization correctness, id allocation safety, and schema evolution strategy to ensure saves remain valid across future sprints that add new LexemeKind variants.
